If by “GTA” you mean the Greater Toronto Area, I’d shortlist agencies that can handle both sides of the problem: Reels/content and a conversion-focused trial page—not just someone who will post three times a week.

My shortlist

ORCAFY Marketing Agency — strong fit for Reels + performance

Etobicoke-based.

Specifically offers vertical video production for Reels/Shorts/Stories, including scripting, filming, editing and posting.

Also does paid social, so they can connect the content to actual enquiries rather than vanity metrics.

Synonym Social — best if creative/social is the bigger weakness

North York-based and explicitly social-first.

Their offering covers scripting, filming, editing and Reels/TikTok-style content, alongside web optimization.

I'd ask them to build the content around your trial offer and objections, rather than generic workout clips.

Charming Media — interesting boutique/wellness option

Particularly relevant because they focus on wellness/fitness/lifestyle brands and have experience with a Toronto fitness-studio launch.

Better fit if your studio needs brand/community positioning as well as social content.

Arnold Street Agency — creative-heavy option

Toronto studio with creative production, digital marketing and web capabilities.

Worth talking to if you want higher-production Reels plus a broader website/brand refresh rather than a narrowly scoped social-media package.

Whissel Strategies - Toronto Marketing Agency — more growth-system oriented

Positions itself around acquisition systems rather than isolated marketing activities.

I'd consider them if the bigger issue is “we get attention but not enough trial bookings.”

One specialist worth looking at

Red Leaf Media — fitness marketing
 is particularly relevant because it works specifically with gyms, fitness studios and personal-training businesses. Its positioning covers training content, trial offers, landing pages, ads and the journey from social attention to enquiry. 
Red Leaf Media

There are also fitness-specific agencies such as LiFet Media
, which explicitly combines fitness lead funnels, trial offers, automated follow-up and social advertising. 
LiFet Media

What I'd actually ask them to pitch

Don't ask for “social media management.” Give each agency the same brief:

Goal: 20–30 qualified trial enquiries/month
Content: 8–12 Reels/month filmed at the studio
Landing page: one dedicated mobile-first trial page
Offer: one clear beginner/trial offer
Measurement: Reel → landing page → enquiry → attended trial → membership

That's important because fitness marketing guidance consistently points toward matching the Reel's promise to a dedicated trial landing page, with one primary CTA and strong local testimonials—not dumping paid/social traffic onto the homepage. 
Zatrovo
+1

If it were my studio, I'd interview ORCAFY, Synonym Social and Red Leaf first. They represent three useful angles: production/performance, social-first creative, and fitness-specific funnel expertise.

If you tell me your studio type (e.g. CrossFit, Pilates, strength, martial arts), approximate monthly marketing budget, and GTA city/neighbourhood, I can narrow this to 3 and compare their services, pricing signals, reviews and relevant case studies.

ChatGPT can make mistakes. Check important info.
